title: Round 12 / algorithm inventor C
question: Collision and search algorithms beyond plain rho: invent algorithms that change the search space or the collision structure (equivalence classes, multi-dimensional walks, structured iteration functions using integer properties of coordinates, batch/preprocessing tradeoffs, adaptive restarts) aiming at a better exponent or constant than Pollard rho on prime-order curves; prototype and benchmark with counted operations.
claims: Experimental (toy prime-order curves, 20-44 bits, counted group ops; pre-registered PROTOCOL.md sha256 d6daf4f1...): reference Pollard rho (DP, r=31) fitted exponent 0.486 (0.467,0.506) in n.

Experimental, NEGATIVE: C1 (negation-class rho with period-2/4 cycle escape, frozen) is not scale-robust: ops/sqrt(n) rises 1.2-1.9 (24-32 bits) to ~11.8 (40 bits), fitted exponent 0.687 (0.652,0.719) on 24-40 bits; 44-bit runs did not finish (censored). Cause: walks trapped in unrecognised fruitless cycles of period >=6.

Experimental, post-hoc amendment C1b (detect any repeat within 16 classes): exponent 0.482 (0.458,0.504); constant-factor gain over ref pooled ~1.13 (95% CI ~0.95-1.33), below the textbook sqrt2; pre-registered constant-factor rule NOT met; no speedup claimed.

Experimental, C2 (preprocessed fixed-walk table, known technique, not novel): online exponent 0.344 (0.317,0.371) with preprocessing exponent 0.62 and memory exponent 0.34; S*T^2/n ~ 4 (slope 0.027), i.e. it sits on the generic S*T^2 ~ N curve; single-query total exponent 0.62 > 1/2; 160/160 queries correct; CI optimistic (one table per size).

Experimental, C3 (multi-instance shared-DP batch, known technique): per-instance cost exponent in n 0.465 (0.455,0.477) at M=16 (unchanged ~1/2); per-instance cost vs M exponent -0.57 (-0.63,-0.50): sqrt(M) law; ref/per-instance 1.7-3.1 at M=16 (strict pre-registered CI rule missed at 32 bits); 138/138 batches correct.

No candidate improved the exponent of the single-instance cost in N below 1/2; all are generic collision algorithms bounded by known generic lower bounds (Shoup; Corrigan-Gibbs-Kogan). Toy-size results are not asymptotic claims.
next_action: PI review of report; if continuing: (1) test non-generic equivalence classes (CM curves j=0/1728, |Aut|=4/6) for realised group-size reduction vs sqrt|Aut|, (2) re-run C1b with larger r to approach sqrt2, (3) any adaptive-restart/new walk candidate must report capped-walk rates vs L. No exponent improvement was found in this territory.
